wrongAnswer.title: Wrong Answer: compare the outputs
wrongAnswer.body: Your code ran, but for at least one case it returned something other than the expected answer. Put the failing case's Expected next to your Output, then follow your code by hand with that input to see where the two part ways.

returnedNothing.title: Your function didn't return anything
returnedNothing.body: CodeBite calls your function with each input and checks what it returns, not what it prints. Hand your answer back with return instead of printing it (print, console.log or System.out.println).

compileError.title: Compile Error: the code couldn't start
compileError.body: Part of the code isn't valid in this language: a typo, a missing bracket or colon, or a wrong type. The red underline in the editor marks the line where it broke, and the message below says why.

runtimeError.title: Runtime Error: the code crashed
runtimeError.body: Your code started but stopped partway through. Common causes are an index out of range (reading past the end of a list), dividing by zero, or using a value that is null or None. The red underline in the editor and the message below point at the line. In Python, a typo such as an unclosed bracket shows up here too, as a SyntaxError.

timeLimitExceeded.title: Time Limit Exceeded: right idea, too slow
timeLimitExceeded.body: Your idea may well be right, but it took too long on the largest inputs. Look for work done over and over, like a loop inside a loop, that a better approach (a hash map, sorting, two pointers) can avoid.

firstAccepted.title: Accepted! Every case passed
firstAccepted.body: A problem solved today counts toward your Streak, the flame in the top bar. Rate how confident you felt, now or later from the Submissions tab, and CodeBite will bring this problem back for review when it's due.

tutorialBanner.label: New to CodeBite?
tutorialBanner.title: New here? Solve your first problem with a guide
tutorialBanner.body: A short tutorial on a very easy problem shows how practising works: what you write, what Run and Submit do, and how to read a result.

read.title: Read the problem
read.body: Start with the description below: what the function gets, what it should give back, the examples and the constraints.

function.title: Fill in the function
function.body: You only write the body of the function in the editor. CodeBite calls it with each input and checks what it returns. Ignore the wrapper around it (such as class Solution), and return your answer: printing it is not an answer.

run.title: Run your code
run.body: Run tries your code on the example cases. It's free and saves nothing, so run as often as you like.

readFailure.title: Read the failure
readFailure.body: The Test panel shows each failing case's Expected output next to yours. Find where they differ, fix the code and Run again.

submit.title: Submit
submit.body: Submit checks every case, hidden ones included, and saves the result to your submission history.

accepted.title: Accepted! You solved your first problem
accepted.body: A problem solved each day keeps your Streak going: the flame in the top bar. Rate how confident you felt, and CodeBite brings the problem back for review when it's due.
